articles.title: Transport workers in Chile block highways in protest over surging fuel prices
articles.summary: Hundreds of bus and lorry drivers are blocking traffic along major highway routes across the country.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Transport workers in Chile block highways in protest over surging fuel prices
articles.summaryTr: Hundreds of bus and lorry drivers are blocking traffic along major highway routes across the country.
articles.articleText: Transport workers in Chile block highways in protest over surging fuel prices - Published Hundreds of transport workers in Chile have blocked roads and highways across the country in protest over high fuel prices. Drivers of busses and lorries began protesting on Tuesday, gathering in convoys to halt traffic along major routes. They are demanding a relief from surging diesel prices, which have been driven up by the war in Iran. Talks between government officials and protest leaders have so far failed to reach a resolution, with another meeting expected to take place on Wednesday. The protest is being organised by the Fuerza del Norte trade union, which represents around 80% of Chile's lorry drivers, and the No+TAG civic protest movement. "There is no point of agreement with the government that could offer any perspective to find solutions for everyone," Andrés Alarcón, a spokesman for No+TAG, said after talks broke down on Tuesday, adding "the strike continues". Economy Minister Daniel Mas called for further dialogue, but warned "at some point, we will have to clear the highways". He stressed the protests were impacting economic activity and exports, saying "we need to get the country moving again". The government of President José Antonio Kast has faced public discontent over fuel prices for months. The average price of diesel has risen 74% since March, according to industry groups. Juan Cornejo, the president of the Association of Intercity Bus Owners, which represents 14 mid-sized companies, told AFP that "we've reached our limit". "We've spent more than a month working with negative numbers," he added. Lorry driver Claudio Elguezabal, who took part in a protest near the capital, Santiago, on Tuesday morning, said the situation was unsustainable. "Right now I'm not making any profit. Sometimes you even have to put in your own money to cover the client," AFP quoted the 47-year-old as saying.

articles.title: Kraken parent adds over 200 tokenized UK and EU stocks to xStocks
articles.summary: The expansion adds more than 200 tokenized UK and EU equities, including all 40 companies in Germany’s DAX index, as xStocks plans further expansion into Hong Kong.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Kraken parent adds over 200 tokenized UK and EU stocks to xStocks
articles.summaryTr: The expansion adds more than 200 tokenized UK and EU equities, including all 40 companies in Germany’s DAX index, as xStocks plans further expansion into Hong Kong.
articles.articleText: Kraken parent adds over 200 tokenized UK and EU stocks to xStocks The expansion adds more than 200 tokenized UK and EU equities, including all 40 companies in Germany’s DAX index, as xStocks plans further expansion into Hong Kong. Kraken parent Payward’s xStocks platform added tokenized versions of more than 200 stocks listed in the United Kingdom and European Union. Payward said Wednesday that eligible users can trade the new tokens on Kraken and participating xStocks Alliance platforms. The tokens remain unavailable to investors in the UK. The expansion includes tokenized shares of all 40 companies in Germany’s benchmark DAX index, including SAP, Siemens, Allianz and Deutsche Telekom. According to a separate Wednesday announcement from Deutsche Börse, the tokens are available for trading on its affiliated 360X platform, with 24/7 trading supported on select venues. Payward said the latest expansion brings xStocks’ offering to more than 1,500 tokenized assets. The company reported more than $45 billion in cumulative transaction volume and over 550,000 unique holders. According to Payward, the new tokens are backed one-to-one by shares held with a regulated custodian. Kraken’s risk disclosure says xStocks tokens give holders exposure to the shares’ performance without voting rights or legal claims to the underlying stock. Token Terminal data put xStocks’ market capitalization at $1.1 billion, about 22% of the $4.9 billion in tokenized stocks the firm tracks. xStocks ranked third, behind Binance bStocks at $1.5 billion and Ondo Finance at $1.4 billion. Payward said it plans to add hundreds of Hong Kong-listed equities in the coming weeks. Related: Kraken launches xChange engine to power tokenized stock trading

articles.title: Eswatini gives illegal foreign businesses 12 months to leave
articles.summary: The law follows the growth of foreign-owned businesses in retail sector in rural areas.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Eswatini gives illegal foreign businesses 12 months to leave
articles.summaryTr: The law follows the growth of foreign-owned businesses in retail sector in rural areas.
articles.articleText: Eswatini gives illegal foreign businesses 12 months to leave - Published Businesses owned by Asian nationals are being closed across Eswatini as the government cracks down on foreign-owned enterprises. The crackdown follows Parliament's approval of the Citizen Economic Empowerment Act, which seeks to increase ownership and participation by emaSwati, as citizens in the kingdom are known. The legislation follows complaints from local traders that foreign-owned businesses are encroaching on traditional retail markets, increasing competition and threatening livelihoods. South Africa has witnessed more severe enforcement actions, including raids, arrests and the disruption of foreign-run informal businesses, while Kenya has also stepped up action against foreign traders. Its implementation has sparked a heated debate in Parliament, with MPs divided over how quickly foreign businesses owners should be required to leave. Mbabane East MP Welcome Dlamini told Parliament on Tuesday that officials from the trade ministry had already begun enforcing the law by closing Asian-owned shops. Hhohho Regional MP Tanele Magagula called for immediate action, saying "Businesses owned by foreigners in the rural areas must be seized immediately." But Dlamini questioned whether local entrepreneurs were ready to take over the businesses, arguing that foreigner should be given time tio train their successors. "Why can't we give the Asians or foreigners at least three years before 'kicking them' out so that emaSwati can learn to run the businesses?" he asked. Magagula rejected the suggestion, questioning why struggling local traders should have to wait while struggling economically. "Why must we wait for three years while emaSwati suffer?" she asked. Parliament subsequently agreed that foreign business owners should be given at least 12 months to leave. However, unless the law is formally amended to reflect that timeline, the ministry could continue enforcing its provisions. The closures follow inspections launched by the trade ministry in August. Some businesses inspected in areas such as Mbabane were found to be fully compliant. However, the inspections also raised concerns about working conditions an administrative practices at foreign-owned enterprises, including complaints by employees over days off, annual leave and overtime. At least one case remains under investigation. Eswatini, a small landlocked kingdom in Southern Africa, faces significant economic hardship, with about 70% of its population living below the poverty line. The government says the new law is intended to expand economic opportunities for citizens, amid concerns that poverty and hunger could fuel further political unrest. The crackdown comes mid growing pressure on foreign-owned businesses elsewhere in the region, particularly in neighbouring South Africa, where anti-immigration campaigns have led to raids, arrests,looting and the disruption of foreign-run informal businesses. On July 30, 2026, the March and March movement intensified its campaign against undocumented immigrants, giving them a deadline to leave. Another protest followed on September 30. The campaigns have been accompanied by violence and attacks on foreign owned businesses. Two Ghanaian and two Nigerian nationals reported killed amid the tensions. Kenya has also stepped up enforcement against foreign traders, bring renewed attention to the treatment of foreign nationals and their businesses across the region. articles.title: Bitcoin short-term holders send 47K BTC to exchanges at a loss
articles.summary: Bitcoin fell to an 11-week low of $72,670 after slipping below short-term holders’ average cost basis of about $75,700, according to CryptoQuant.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Bitcoin short-term holders send 47K BTC to exchanges at a loss
articles.summaryTr: Bitcoin fell to an 11-week low of $72,670 after slipping below short-term holders’ average cost basis of about $75,700, according to CryptoQuant.
articles.articleText: Bitcoin short-term holders send 47K BTC to exchanges at a loss Bitcoin fell to an 11-week low of $72,670 after slipping below short-term holders’ average cost basis of about $75,700, according to CryptoQuant. Bitcoin (BTC) short-term holders sent more than 47,000 BTC to exchanges on Tuesday as Bitcoin fell to an 11-week low, with the coins worth less than their purchase price. Key points: - Short-term holders moved 47,025 BTC to exchanges while the coins were worth less than their acquisition price. - The 24-hour total was the third-highest since July, according to CryptoQuant. - CryptoQuant’s Julio Moreno said a sustained break below $73,000 and a failed rebound above that level would strengthen the case that Bitcoin’s broader downtrend was continuing. Short-term holders’ underwater exchange inflows rank third since July Data from onchain analytics platform CryptoQuant showed short-term holders sent 47,025 BTC carrying unrealized losses to exchanges in the 24 hours to midnight UTC at the start of Wednesday. The tally was among the largest 24-hour totals in the four months of data tracked by CryptoQuant and came as Bitcoin dropped to $72,670, its lowest level since Aug. 20. The short-term holder metric tracks Bitcoin held for up to 155 days. Short-term holders are generally considered more likely to sell when prices fall, even at a loss. “On November 10, profitable transfers stood near 1,700 BTC, meaning approximately 27 BTC arrived at a loss for every 1 BTC transferred at a profit,” CryptoQuant said. The largest 24-hour inflows of BTC carrying unrealized losses since late July occurred on Oct. 8, hours after Bitcoin fell back to $80,000. Rolling 24-hour inflows peaked at 50,500 BTC. Short-term holders’ exchange inflows of BTC carrying unrealized losses. Source: CryptoQuant CryptoQuant analyst flags $73,000 as Bitcoin tests August lows Cointelegraph previously reported that short-term holders’ average cost basis was around $75,700. Related: Stock ETF buyers pounce on dip as Bitcoin funds bleed $1.6 billion Short-term holders moved into an aggregate unrealized profit on Aug. 20 as Bitcoin rebounded toward $80,000. They slipped back into an aggregate unrealized loss on Friday. STH cost basis vs. BTC/USD. Source: CryptoQuant CryptoQuant head of research Julio Moreno said Bitcoin could still be in the downtrend that began in November 2025. “If rallies keep stalling near the cohort’s cost basis and net unrealized losses deepen, the August rebound starts to look like a pause in the broader downtrend,” he wrote on Monday. “A sustained break below $73,000 followed by a failed retest from below would strengthen the case for bear-market continuation.” STH-NUPL vs. BTC/USD. Source: CryptoQuant CryptoQuant’s net unrealized profit/loss (NUPL) metric showed that short-term holders reached their highest level of unrealized profitability since November 2025 as Bitcoin climbed to $87,200 in September.

articles.title: Poundland set for more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue
articles.summary: The BBC understands the discount chain, which has been edging towards administration, will be given more time to find a buyer.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Poundland set for more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue
articles.summaryTr: The BBC understands the discount chain, which has been edging towards administration, will be given more time to find a buyer.
articles.articleText: Poundland set for more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue - Published Poundland and its 11,000 employees are hopeful that the retailer's impending collapse can be delayed to allow time for a last-minute rescue deal. The discount chain has been edging towards administration after being blocked by its owners from accessing cash in its bank accounts. A deadline to secure a buyer for the business is set to expire at midnight, but sources close to the situation have told the BBC that they expect more time will be given, thanks to the release of £10m in funding. A committee of MPs is set to question Gordon Brothers, Poundland's US owners, on Wednesday following accusations that the investment firm hopes to profit from selling off Poundland's 600 stores and stock piecemeal. Gordon Brothers - which bought the chain for just £1 last year - is accused of forcing that outcome by restricting Poundland's access to available cash needed to restock stores and pay wages and rent, ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period. The investment firm has denied the claims. But pressure remains on Poundland's owners after a takeover bid was rejected. The decision prompted calls for answers from politicians, including Prime Minister Andy Burnham. About £50m had been frozen by Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning Poundland bosses were unable to restock shelves across its 600 shops. However, sources close to the matter told the BBC on Tuesday that a release of £10m by its owners, while "small in the scale of things" could help at least postpone the chain's collapse while a longer term solution was explored. Views on Poundland performance differ The 10-day moratorium to protect Poundland from its creditors expires on Thursday, but if there is a prospect of a solvent deal, the deadline could be extended. Views on the chain's performance differ between those running operations and the owners. Poundland boss Barry Williams told staff last week that like-for-like sales, which exclude new store openings, were up 11.4%. The sales period included Halloween, but Williams said this was £1.5m ahead of budget. He added the business made a profit of £18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year where there were losses of £68m. However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading". There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up Poundland stores which could mean continuing employment for workers in the event the chain is broken up and sold off in chunks. The main issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland as a national chain. Get in touch Are you affected by issues discussed in this story? He added the business made a profit of £18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year where there were losses of £68m. However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading". There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up Poundland stores which could mean continuing employment for workers in the event the chain is broken up and sold off in chunks. The main issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland as a national chain. Get in touch Are you affected by issues discussed in this story? articles.title: Bitget Wallet reports sevenfold jump in crypto phishing risk alerts
articles.summary: The wallet flagged about 37,000 signing requests a week for phishing in Q3 and said better monitoring likely contributed to the increase.

articles.titleTr: Bitget Wallet reports sevenfold jump in crypto phishing risk alerts
articles.summaryTr: The wallet flagged about 37,000 signing requests a week for phishing in Q3 and said better monitoring likely contributed to the increase.
articles.articleText: Bitget Wallet reports sevenfold jump in crypto phishing risk alerts The wallet flagged about 37,000 signing requests a week for phishing in Q3 and said better monitoring likely contributed to the increase. Crypto wallet provider Bitget Wallet said Wednesday it was expanding AI-assisted threat detection after its weekly average of signing requests flagged for potential phishing rose 7.4-fold in the third quarter of 2026. The wallet flagged about 37,000 such requests per week in Q3, up from 5,000 in Q2, according to Bitget Wallet chief operating officer Alvin Kan. “The increase likely reflects both greater threat activity and improved detection capabilities, although the data does not allow us to quantify each factor’s contribution,” Kan told Cointelegraph. The wallet introduced AI-assisted risk detection in Q2, he added. Kan said that the tally counted flagged signing interactions, not unique attacks or confirmed financial losses. Bitget Wallet said its expanded AI checks examine website code and domain registration details for signs of fraud. The wallet also simulates transactions to spot hidden permissions before users sign. Bitget Wallet also said AI helped identify 90% of newly blocked risky domains in October, compared with 36% in Q2. Nearly 70% of domains its AI flagged that month had no matching alerts in the external threat feeds it checked. The findings come amid continued phishing threats targeting crypto users. In July, a trader lost nearly $1 million after signing a malicious Ethereum token approval. An August investigation by Rapid7 uncovered a phishing campaign that targeted 885,000 phone numbers and directed recipients to websites impersonating crypto wallet providers. Related: Phishing, deepfakes, supply chain attacks to fuel 2026’s biggest crypto hacks: CertiK

articles.title: Tearful Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands
articles.summary: Tatjana Smith, South Africa's most decorated Olympian, switches allegiance to the Netherlands.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Tearful Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands
articles.summaryTr: Tatjana Smith, South Africa's most decorated Olympian, switches allegiance to the Netherlands.
articles.articleText: Tearful Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands - Published South Africa's most decorated Olympian Tatjana Smith was in tears as she announced that she has switched allegiance to the Netherlands. The 29-year-old won four Olympic breaststroke medals, including two golds, before retiring after the Paris 2024 Games. She came out of retirement in September and hopes to compete in the 50m breaststroke as the event makes its Olympic debut at the 2028 Games in Los Angeles. Smith, whose maiden name was Schoenmaker, wiped away tears as she read a letter addressed to South Africa, saying that "dreams can change as we grow". Smith has dual citizenship because her father is Dutch. She said she has "always been Dutch and South African" and that this is an opportunity to "explore another part of my identity and heritage that I've never experienced through sport". She said it also offers her "greater high-performance support and the potential to build a more sustainable career" because the "financial and practical challenges of swimming were among the reasons my previous career became difficult to sustain". Smith has previously said that financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, contributed to her decision to step away from the sport. Swimming South Africa has been approached for comment. Smith won four world and Commonwealth gold medals between 2018 and 2023. She won gold in the 200m breaststroke and 100m silver at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, before adding 100m gold and 200m silver in 2024. "Representing South Africa was a childhood dream come true, and it's a chapter I will always look back on with immense pride and gratitude," she said on social media., external "The people, the memories and everything we achieved together will always be part of me. But dreams can change as we grow. "This next chapter is about embracing another part of who I am, falling in love with the journey and discovering what more I'm capable of. "I'm excited for what lies ahead, and I truly hope you'll continue to be part of the journey with me." Smith, who said she will continue to live and train in South Africa, is set to represent the Netherlands for the first time at the short course World Championships from 1-6 December. She acknowledged that her switch "may disappoint or break the hearts" of some supporters. The Ministry of Sport, Arts and Culture in South Africa said it was aware of the "problems at Swimming South Africa". "The country was delighted to see her return to the pool, but South Africa does not own her," a statement read. "Tatjana's choice belongs to her and it should not be turned into a political weapon." Gayton McKenzie, Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture, said: "Every medal, every record and every anthem she gave us belongs to our history forever. We now have to share her with the Netherlands."

articles.title: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
articles.articleText: Release Number 9324-26 CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers November 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced eight orders filing and settling charges against Michael Talento, Anthony Tyler Williams, Quillan Roberto Black, Christopher Williams, Michael Levi Peters, Jordan Taylor Morgan, Lewis Matthew Neal, and Tyler Evan MacKechnie for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
articles.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
articles.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

articles.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

news.summary: Dünya Varlık Yönetim AŞ, 11 Şubat 2026'da ihraç ettiği 100 milyon TL tutarındaki tahvilin üçüncü kupon ödemesi vadesinde yapılamadı.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Dünya Varlık Yönetim kupon ödemesinde temerrüde düştü
news.summaryTr: Dünya Varlık Yönetim AŞ, 11 Şubat 2026'da ihraç ettiği 100 milyon TL tutarındaki tahvilin üçüncü kupon ödemesi vadesinde yapılamadı.
news.articleText: Dünya Varlık Yönetim kupon ödemesinde temerrüde düştü YAYIN TARİHİ, 11 Kasım 2026 16:01 PAYLAŞ - Dünya Varlık Yönetim AŞ, 11 Şubat 2026'da ihraç ettiği 100 milyon TL tutarındaki tahvilin üçüncü kupon ödemesi vadesinde yapılamadı. Dünya Varlık Yönetim AŞ, 11 Kasım 2026 tarihinde vadesi gelen tahvil kupon ödemesini gerçekleştiremediğini Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) açıkladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirketin 11 Şubat 2026 tarihinde ihraç ettiği 100 milyon TL tutarındaki tahvilin üçüncü kupon ödemesi kapsamında 10,9 milyon TL ödeme yapılması gerekiyordu. Ancak söz konusu tutar vadesinde ödenemedi. Dünya Varlık Yönetim, aynı tahvil için mayıs ayında 11,5 milyon TL, ağustos ayında ise 11,7 milyon TL tutarında kupon ödemesi gerçekleştirmişti. Kaynak: cnbce.com

news.summary: Fon soruşturmasında tutuklanan Ali Paslı, Yunus Arıncı ve Ömer Murat Gülkan hakkındaki savcılık sevk yazısında dikkat çeken tespitler yer aldı. Yazıda 2,4 milyar liralık fon kazancı, 500 bin dolarlık rüşvet ve 3,8 milyar liralık VDMK işlemlerine ilişkin iddialar aktarıldı.

news.articleText: Fon soruşturması: 3 ismin sevk yazısında 2,4 milyar liralık kazanç ve 500 bin dolarlık rüşvet iddiası - Fon soruşturmasında tutuklanan Ali Paslı, Yunus Arıncı ve Ömer Murat Gülkan hakkındaki savcılık sevk yazısında dikkat çeken tespitler yer aldı. Yazıda 2,4 milyar liralık fon kazancı, 500 bin dolarlık rüşvet ve 3,8 milyar liralık VDMK işlemlerine ilişkin iddialar aktarıldı. Sermaye piyasalarında gerçekleştirilen işlemlere ilişkin yürütülen fon soruşturması devam ediyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Soruşturma kapsamında tutuklanan Ali Paslı, Yunus Arıncı ve Ömer Murat Gülkan hakkındaki savcılığın sevk yazısında şüphelilere dair tespitler yer aldı. İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığınca, sermaye piyasalarında gerçekleştirilen işlemlere ilişkin fon soruşturması devam ediyor. Adil Katılım Bankası'nın 2,4 milyar liralık fon kazancı mercek altında Soruşturma kapsamında tutuklanan OMG Capital Advisors Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Ömer Murat Gülkan, eski Takasbank Genel Müdürü Yunus Arıncı ile Adil Katılım Bankası ortaklarından Ali Paslı hakkında savcılığın tutuklama talebinde bulunduğu sevk yazısına ulaşıldı. Yazıda, Ali Paslı'nın kurucularından ve pay sahiplerinden olduğu Adil Katılım Bankasının 31 Temmuz 2025'te şirket sermayesinden 1 milyar 844 milyon lira tutarında TLY fonu satın aldığı kaydedildi. Aynı fonların 23 Ekim 2025'te satıldığı ve toplamda yaklaşık 2 milyar 430 milyon lira kar elde edildiği aktarılan yazıda, kuruluş aşamasındaki bir bankanın sermayesinin yarısından fazlasını, TEFAS'ta yeni işlem görmeye başlamış ve geçmiş performansı bulunmayan tek bir fona yatırmasının risk yoğunlaşması ve likidite yönetimi bakımından izah edilemez nitelikte olduğu vurgulandı. Yazıda, yaklaşık 2 aylık süreçte bu denli yüksek kar elde edilmesinin hayatın olağan akışına uygun olmadığı belirtilerek, elde edilen getirinin, aynı dönemde piyasa koşullarıyla uyumsuz olduğu dile getirildi. Dosyaya 6 Kasım'da gelen MASAK raporuna göre, bankanın Tera fonlarına yatırdığı paranın yine Tera Yatırım Bankası AŞ tarafından Ali Emre Ballı'nın (aracında ölü bulunan Finansal Kurumlar Birliği Başkanı) bağlantılı şirketlerine verilen kredilerle sağlandığının anlaşıldığı ifade edildi. Yunus Arıncı hakkındaki 500 bin dolarlık rüşvet aldığı iddiası Yazıda, Takasbank'ın eski genel müdürü olan şüpheli Yunus Arıncı'nın bu görevi sırasında Tera Yatırım temsilcileri Erdin Özel ve Emir Münir Sarpyener ile irtibat halinde bulunduğu belirtilerek, şüphelinin Umut Güner (Dünya Gazetesi'nin ortaklarından) aracılığıyla 500 bin dolar rüşvet aldığına dair ifade bulunduğu aktarıldı. Ayrıca Güner'den 4 milyon 500 bin lira alan Arıncı'nın görevinin sağladığı gücü kötüye kullanarak bu miktarı iade etmediğine dair kuvvetli suç şüphesi bulunduğu vurgulandı. Yazıda, bunlara ek olarak, Tera grubunun Katılımevim'i devralması sürecinde Yunus Arıncı'nın BDDK'nin yönlendirmesiyle kredi artışı yaptığına dair beyan bulunduğu ifade edilerek, toplanan deliller birlikte değerlendirildiğinde, şüphelinin üzerine atılı suçu işlediği yönünde kuvvetli suç şüphesini gösteren somut deliller olduğu kaydedildi. Şüpheli Ömer Murat Gülkan'ın ise OMG Yönetim ve Danışmanlık AŞ'nin yüzde 65 ortağı ve imza yetkilisi olduğu anlatılan yazıda, Sermaye Piyasası Kurulundan (SPK) herhangi bir izni bulunmayan şirketi aracılığıyla, yazılı sözleşme olmaksızın Türkiye Sigorta, Türkiye Hayat ve BES fonundan şirket hesabına para alarak 2022-2026 döneminde toplam 3,8 milyar lira tutarında VDMK işlemi gerçekleştirdiği belirtildi. Yazıda, şüphelinin kendi beyanına göre bu işlemlerden yaklaşık 100 milyon liradan fazla kazanç elde ettiği aktarılarak, bu hususun MKK kayıtları ve Gülkan'ın ikrarıyla sabit olduğu, şüphelinin söz konusu gelirleri sisteme entegre ederek üzerine atılı suçu işlediği yönünde kuvvetli suç şüphesi bulunduğu vurgulandı. Hakimlik, şüpheliler Yunus Arıncı, Ali Paslı ve Ömer Murat Gülkan'ın tutuklanmasına karar vermişti. Diğer şüpheliler Enver Çevik, Nureddin Çevik, Kemal Akkaya ve Ayhan Yazkan hakkında ise adli kontrol tedbiri uygulanmıştı.

news.summaryTr: Elon Musk'ın uzay şirketi SpaceX, uydularında kullanılacak güneş hücrelerinin üretimi için Alman Singulus Technologies ile anlaşma yaptı. 2027'nin ilk yarısında teslim edilmesi planlanan üretim hattının, şirketin 100 GW'lık üretim hedefini desteklemesi bekleniyor.
news.articleText: SpaceX'ten Almanya'ya dev güneş enerjisi siparişi: Hedef 100 GW üretim - Elon Musk'ın uzay şirketi SpaceX, uydularında kullanılacak güneş hücrelerinin üretimi için Alman Singulus Technologies ile anlaşma yaptı. - 2027'nin ilk yarısında teslim edilmesi planlanan üretim hattının, şirketin 100 GW'lık üretim hedefini desteklemesi bekleniyor. Elon Musk'ın sahibi olduğu SpaceX, uzay tabanlı güneş enerjisi üretimini büyütmek için Almanya merkezli Singulus Technologies ile tedarik anlaşması imzaladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Anlaşma kapsamında Singulus, SpaceX'e heteroeklem (HJT) güneş hücrelerinin üretiminde kullanılacak anahtar teslim bir üretim hattı sağlayacak. Şirketler arasındaki stratejik ortaklığın yalnızca bu hatla sınırlı kalmayacağı, ilerleyen dönemde birden fazla ek üretim hattının da teslim edilmesinin planlandığı belirtildi. Üretim hattı 2027'nin ilk yarısında teslim edilecek Singulus Technologies, üretim hattını 2027'nin ilk yarısında teslim edecek. Üretimin aşamalı olarak artırılması ve SpaceX'in 100 GW'ın üzerindeki üretim ekipmanı hedefine destek verilmesi planlanıyor. SpaceX'in Teksas'ın Bastrop kentindeki tesisinde Starmind uydularının üretimini hızlandırdığı belirtiliyor. Yeni anlaşma, şirketin uydu üretim kapasitesini artırma planları kapsamında önem taşıyor. Singulus Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Lars Lieberwirth, şirketin ıslak kimya, vakum kaplama ve termal işlem teknolojilerini bir araya getiren üretim yaklaşımının sektörde farklılaşmalarını sağladığını söyledi. Lieberwirth, SpaceX ile ortaklığın bu teknolojilerin büyük ölçekte sanayileştirilmesine katkı sunacağını ifade etti. Musk'ın güneş enerjisi yatırımları büyüyor SpaceX ile yapılan anlaşma, Musk'ın güneş enerjisi üretimine yönelik yatırımlarının gündemde olduğu bir dönemde geldi. Reuters, daha önce Tesla'nın Çinli üreticilerden yaklaşık 3 milyar dolarlık güneş enerjisi üretim ekipmanı satın almak üzere görüşmeler yürüttüğünü bildirmişti. Bu süreçte Singulus ile SpaceX, Mart 2026'da stratejik ortaklığa gitmiş ve Alman şirkete önemli miktarda finansman sağlanmıştı. Geçen ay ise Singulus'a teminatlı ve ikincil nitelikte yeni bir kredi desteği sunulmuştu. Teksas Denetçisi'ne sunulan başvuru belgelerine göre Tesla, 100 GW kapasiteli ve üretimin tüm aşamalarını kapsayan güneş enerjisi projesine 10,1 milyar dolar yatırım yapmayı hedefliyor. PV-Tech'in haberine göre projede ticari üretimin 2029'un ilk çeyreğinde başlaması öngörülüyor. Uydularda HJT güneş hücrelerine ilgi artıyor Uzay uygulamalarında güneş hücresi teknolojileri de dönüşüm geçiriyor. Uydularda bugün ağırlıklı olarak kullanılan galyum arsenit hücreler yüksek performans sunarken, maliyetleri silikon tabanlı alternatiflere kıyasla oldukça yüksek. SpaceX ve Amazon gibi şirketlerin uydu sayısını artırması, daha düşük maliyetli silikon tabanlı güneş hücrelerine yönelik ilgiyi yükseltiyor. Sektörde, önümüzdeki beş yıl içinde alçak Dünya yörüngesindeki uydularda silikon teknolojisinin yaygınlaşabileceği ve HJT hücrelerin öne çıkabileceği değerlendiriliyor. SpaceX'in Starlink bölümünden Sorumlu Kıdemli Başkan Yardımcısı Mike Nicolls da Singulus ortaklığının Teksas'taki Starmind uydu tesisinde yüksek performanslı güneş hücresi üretimi için yeni bir yol açacağını belirtti. HJT (heteroeklem) teknolojisi, farklı silikon katmanlarını bir araya getirerek güneş hücrelerinin verimliliğini artırmayı hedefliyor. Teknoloji, yüksek performans ve üretim maliyetlerini dengeleme potansiyeli nedeniyle uzay uygulamalarında da ilgi görüyor.

news.title: Kenya discharges last Ebola patient in key milestone to being declared free of the virus
news.summary: The country begins a 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free, provided no new cases are recorded.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Kenya discharges last Ebola patient in key milestone to being declared free of the virus
news.summaryTr: The country begins a 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free, provided no new cases are recorded.
news.articleText: Kenya discharges last Ebola patient in key milestone to being declared free of the virus - Published Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient - the seventh to recover from the virus - marking a major milestone in efforts to contain the disease in the East African nation, which now begins a 42-day countdown to officially being declared Ebola-free. It had confirmed its first ever case of Ebola early in October when a Kenyan businessman died within days of arriving in the capital, Nairobi. He had contracted the virus in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where more than 5,000 people have died in an ongoing outbreak that began in May. His mother also subsequently died. Kenya's health minister said 135 identified contacts of the infected patients had also completed their 21 days in isolation. "Today with the discharge of the last patient we can confirm and tell the world that seven patients have recovered - and all contacts have completed their follow-up monitoring," Aden Duale said. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) described it as an important achievement in the regional response to the outbreak. "This is an encouraging moment for Kenya and for Africa. We must sustain surveillance and vigilance until the outbreak is officially declared over," Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya posted on X. - What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult? - Published15 September Kenya has reported no new confirmed cases since 20 October. All the Kenyan cases were linked to the man who had travelled from DR Congo through Uganda, with health officials reporting no evidence of wider community transmission. Those who have recovered following treatment included four healthcare workers. Five patients were discharged on 3 November, followed by a sixth three days later, before the final patient was cleared on Wednesday. Under World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines, 42 days must pass after the last patient tests negative and is discharged, or the last Ebola victim is safely buried, before an outbreak can be declared over. The Ebola virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days, meaning those exposed to the virus may not become ill for several weeks. Duale said the government would maintain heightened surveillance at border crossings, airports, health facilities and communities throughout the countdown. Emergency response teams will remain on alert across the country, while the health authorities will continue monitoring travellers arriving from affected countries. Kenyans returning from Ebola-affected areas are required to complete electronic health declarations before travelling, undergo screening on arrival and spend 21 days in quarantine under the supervision of health teams. The minister also urged countries that had imposed travel and visa restrictions to reconsider them - adding that Kenya had no intention of serving as a quarantine centre for another country. In May, a Kenyan court suspended US plans to open an Ebola quarantine facility for American citizens. Kenya has maintained that there is no need to restrict domestic travel, trade or public gatherings. The outbreak has nevertheless disrupted international travel, with some Gulf countries introducing restrictions affecting travellers from Kenya and other African countries. Saudi Arabia stopped issuing visas to Kenyan nationals in late October, prompting concerns among those seeking employment there. Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) has announced that it is lifting its suspension on issuing new visas to Ugandan nationals, easing restrictions introduced in June. But Ugandans will have to spend at least 21 days outside of Uganda before being allowed to travel to the UAE. The UAE is also allowing certain students, diplomatic passport holders and Ugandan embassy employees to enter under approved health procedures. Uganda, which shares a long and busy border with DR Congo, was among the countries first affected but declared its own Ebola outbreak over on 27 August. The current outbreak in DR Congo has been caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way. - Ebola outbreak in DR Congo becomes deadliest in its history - Published17 August Go to BBCAfrica.com, external for more news from the African continent. news.title: What are cold weather payments and who can get them?
news.summary: Some people in England, Wales and Northern Ireland can get help with heating costs during cold spells.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: What are cold weather payments and who can get them?
news.summaryTr: Some people in England, Wales and Northern Ireland can get help with heating costs during cold spells.
news.articleText: What are cold weather payments and who can get them? - Published As temperatures drop, heating costs rise, but there is some help for many households through cold weather payments. This financial help is triggered across hundreds of postcodes in England, Wales and Northern Ireland when there is a prolonged period of below-zero temperatures. In Scotland, those on low incomes and benefits may receive a separate winter heating payment, which does not depend on how cold it gets. What are cold weather payments? The cold weather payment is a government benefit top-up to help with fuel bills, external. The average temperature in a local area must be recorded as, or forecast to be, 0C or below for seven days in a row. The temperature is recorded by the relevant weather station for your postcode. - England and Wales: Enter your postcode here to check eligibility, external - Northern Ireland: Enter your postcode here to check eligibility, external More than 1.4 million cold weather payments were made during winter 2025-26. Who can get cold weather payments and how much are they worth? To qualify, you must live in England, Wales or Northern Ireland. Payments are not age-related but you must already be receiving certain benefits, including: - pension credit - income support - income-based job seekers' allowance - income-related employment and support allowance - universal credit - although there are certain exceptions - support for mortgage interest Each cold weather payment is for a seven-day period and is worth £25. More than one payment will be made during the course of the winter if there are enough periods of cold weather. The scheme runs between 1 November and 31 March each year. Hospital stays can affect your entitlement to the payment so you should tell the Pension Service, external or Jobcentre Plus, external if you become an inpatient. You should also update the relevant service if you have a baby, or if a child under five comes to live with you. In Scotland, the winter heating payment is worth £62, external, and is paid automatically between December and February. - Heating tips to keep your home warm when budgets are squeezed - Published2 January - How to keep babies warm in cold weather and other winter tips - Published2 January - How to drive in snow and icy weather - Published2 January - How do cold weather health alerts work? - Published22 June How do I get cold weather payments and how long does it take? You do not have to do anything in order to receive cold weather payments. The money should be paid automatically into the same bank or building society account as your benefits, within two weeks of the qualifying period of cold weather. If you do not receive a payment, you can contact the Pension Service, external or Jobcentre Plus, external. Cold weather payments do not affect other benefits. They are separate to the winter fuel payment, which is worth £100 or £300 depending on your individual circumstances. About nine million pensioners get the Winter Fuel Payment, after a government u-turn over changes to the eligibility rules.

news.title: Altın ticaretinde dengeler değişiyor: 500 tonluk merkez için düğmeye basıldı
news.summary: Küresel altın ticaretinde Asya'nın ağırlığı artarken Singapur'dan dikkat çeken bir adım geldi. Ülke, merkez bankaları için 500 ton kapasiteli altın saklama hizmeti başlatırken, vergi teşvikleriyle Londra ve İsviçre'ye alternatif olmayı hedefliyor.

news.titleTr: Altın ticaretinde dengeler değişiyor: 500 tonluk merkez için düğmeye basıldı
news.summaryTr: Küresel altın ticaretinde Asya'nın ağırlığı artarken Singapur'dan dikkat çeken bir adım geldi. Ülke, merkez bankaları için 500 ton kapasiteli altın saklama hizmeti başlatırken, vergi teşvikleriyle Londra ve İsviçre'ye alternatif olmayı hedefliyor.
news.articleText: Altın ticaretinde dengeler değişiyor: 500 tonluk merkez için düğmeye basıldı - Küresel altın ticaretinde Asya'nın ağırlığı artarken Singapur'dan dikkat çeken bir adım geldi. Ülke, merkez bankaları için 500 ton kapasiteli altın saklama hizmeti başlatırken, vergi teşvikleriyle Londra ve İsviçre'ye alternatif olmayı hedefliyor. Singapur Para Otoritesi (MAS), yabancı merkez bankaları ve devlet kuruluşlarına yönelik yeni altın saklama hizmetini devreye aldı. Başlangıç kapasitesi 500 metrik ton olan hizmetle, ülkelerin altın rezervlerini farklı merkezlerde değerlendirmelerine olanak sağlanması amaçlanıyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Singapur yönetimi ayrıca altın depolama, rafine etme, yeniden döküm, test ve aracılık gibi toptan hizmetlere vergi muafiyetleri getirmeyi planlıyor. Ülkede fiziksel altın işlemlerini kolaylaştıracak yeni takas sisteminin ise 2027'nin ilk çeyreğinde faaliyete geçmesi bekleniyor. Altın ticaretinin merkezi Asya'ya kayıyor Singapur'un hamlesi, küresel altın ticaretinde Asya'nın ağırlığının giderek arttığı bir döneme denk geliyor. Geleneksel olarak Londra ve İsviçre üzerinden gerçekleşen altın işlemleri, Asya'daki rafineri kapasitesinin genişlemesi ve bölgesel talebin yükselmesiyle dönüşüm geçiriyor. Ancak Singapur'un köklü merkezlerle rekabet etmesi kolay görünmüyor. Ekim sonu itibarıyla Londra'daki kasalarda yaklaşık 9 bin 850 ton altın bulunurken, Singapur'un yeni hizmetinin başlangıç kapasitesi 500 ton seviyesinde. Merkez bankalarının altın rezervleri için yeni adres Dünya Altın Konseyi'nin küresel merkez bankaları başkanı Shaokai Fan, jeopolitik gerilimlerin ülkeleri altın rezervlerini nerede saklayacaklarını yeniden değerlendirmeye yönelttiğini belirtti. Fan'a göre Singapur'un siyasi istikrarı, güçlü hukuki altyapısı ve ulaşım bağlantıları, ülkeyi merkez bankaları açısından cazip bir alternatif haline getirebilir. Metals Focus Genel Müdürü Nikolas Kavalis ise yalnızca altın depolama kapasitesinin yeterli olmayacağına dikkat çekti. Kavalis, Londra ile rekabet edebilmek için güçlü bir işlem hacmi ve likidite oluşturulması gerektiğini vurguladı. news.title: FSB urgest Turkey to tighten crypto oversight, set stablecoin rules
news.summary: The Financial Stability Board cited progress on crypto licensing and urged stronger enforcement and cooperation with foreign regulators.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: FSB urgest Turkey to tighten crypto oversight, set stablecoin rules
news.summaryTr: The Financial Stability Board cited progress on crypto licensing and urged stronger enforcement and cooperation with foreign regulators.
news.articleText: FSB urgest Turkey to tighten crypto oversight, set stablecoin rules The Financial Stability Board cited progress on crypto licensing and urged stronger enforcement and cooperation with foreign regulators. The Financial Stability Board (FSB) urged Turkey to tighten its oversight of crypto markets and adopt dedicated rules for stablecoins. In a peer review published on Wednesday, the global financial watchdog said Turkish authorities had made progress by introducing registration and licensing requirements for crypto service providers. The report was part of the FSB’s regular program of country reviews and assessed Turkey’s progress in implementing the board’s 2023 global recommendations on crypto and stablecoins. It followed a broader 2025 review that found gaps in how jurisdictions had implemented those recommendations. The FSB recommended that Turkey begin monitoring crypto-related risks to financial stability under a formal framework, strengthen supervision and enforcement, and improve cooperation and information sharing with foreign regulators. Turkey’s Capital Markets Board introduced licensing and operational requirements for crypto exchanges and custodians in March 2025, including minimum capital thresholds. The FSB said Turkey had introduced safeguards including requirements to segregate assets held in custody and a ban on domestic crypto payments. The safeguards help limit the spread of crypto-related risks to banks and payment systems. Authorities also launched a centralized platform to monitor crypto activities. The FSB’s 2025 review found that Turkey had finalized rules for crypto assets but lacked a dedicated stablecoin framework. In June 2025, Turkey’s Finance Ministry outlined plans to introduce additional transaction checks and limits on stablecoin transfers to combat money laundering. news.title: Volkswagen'de kriz büyüyor: Ana fabrikadaki dev proje iptal edildi
news.summary: Alman otomotiv devi Volkswagen, Wolfsburg'daki ana fabrikasında hayata geçirmeyi planladığı üretim projesini iptal etti. Elektrikli Golf kararının ardından gelen yeni hamle, 100 bin kişilik işten çıkarma planına karşı çıkan işçi temsilcileriyle gerilimi artırdı.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Volkswagen'de kriz büyüyor: Ana fabrikadaki dev proje iptal edildi
news.summaryTr: Alman otomotiv devi Volkswagen, Wolfsburg'daki ana fabrikasında hayata geçirmeyi planladığı üretim projesini iptal etti. Elektrikli Golf kararının ardından gelen yeni hamle, 100 bin kişilik işten çıkarma planına karşı çıkan işçi temsilcileriyle gerilimi artırdı.
news.articleText: Volkswagen'de kriz büyüyor: Ana fabrikadaki dev proje iptal edildi - Alman otomotiv devi Volkswagen, Wolfsburg'daki ana fabrikasında hayata geçirmeyi planladığı üretim projesini iptal etti. Elektrikli Golf kararının ardından gelen yeni hamle, 100 bin kişilik işten çıkarma planına karşı çıkan işçi temsilcileriyle gerilimi artırdı. Avrupa'nın en büyük otomobil üreticisi Volkswagen, maliyetleri azaltmaya ve operasyonlarını yeniden yapılandırmaya yönelik adımlarına bir yenisini ekledi. Şirket, Almanya'nın Wolfsburg kentindeki ana üretim tesisinde uygulanması planlanan ve gelecekteki otomobil modellerinin üretim süreçlerine temel oluşturması beklenen "Gamechanger" projesinden vazgeçti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Reuters'e e-posta yoluyla açıklama yapan Volkswagen Grubu, söz konusu üretim konseptinin başlangıçta öngörüldüğü şekilde uygulanmayacağını bildirdi. Elektrikli Golf kararının ardından yeni adım Volkswagen'in son kararı, tamamen elektrikli Golf modelinin Wolfsburg'daki geliştirme çalışmalarını askıya aldığını duyurmasından iki haftadan kısa bir süre sonra geldi. Art arda açıklanan kararlar, şirketin maliyet düşürme ve küçülme stratejisinin Almanya'daki merkez fabrikasını da doğrudan etkilemeye başladığını gösterdi. 100 bin kişilik işten çıkarma planı CEO Oliver Blume yönetimindeki Volkswagen, özellikle Çinli otomobil üreticilerinden gelen yoğun rekabet ve artan maliyetler nedeniyle kapsamlı bir yeniden yapılanma sürecinden geçiyor. Şirket yönetiminin planları arasında 100 bin çalışanın işten çıkarılması ve Almanya'daki dört üretim tesisinin kapatılması bulunuyor. Ancak bu adımlar, Volkswagen'in güçlü sendikaları ve işçi temsilcilerinin sert tepkisiyle karşılaşıyor. Sendikalar, yönetimin mevcut yaklaşımını değiştirmemesi halinde 1 Ocak'tan itibaren greve gidilebileceği uyarısında bulunuyor. İşçi temsilcilerinden anlaşma ihlali uyarısı Volkswagen İşçi Konseyi Başkanı Daniela Cavallo, Gamechanger projesinin iptal edilmesini şirket yönetimi ile çalışanlar arasında daha önce varılan uzlaşmadan ciddi bir geri adım olarak değerlendirdi. Cavallo, Aralık 2024'te imzalanan anlaşmanın, yeniden yapılanma ve işten çıkarmalar karşılığında yatırım ve istihdam güvenceleri içerdiğini hatırlattı. Yeni kararın söz konusu anlaşmanın temel unsurlarıyla çeliştiğini savunan Cavallo, yönetimin çalışanlara verdiği taahhütlerden uzaklaştığını belirtti. İşçi temsilcileri ise Volkswagen'in yatırım ve istihdam güvencelerine ilişkin yükümlülüklerini yerine getirmeme riskiyle karşı karşıya olduğunu ileri sürdü. Volkswagen'de yönetim ve çalışanlar arasındaki gerilim büyüyor Alman otomotiv devinin üretim planlarında yaptığı değişiklikler, yeniden yapılanma sürecinin yalnızca maliyetleri azaltmakla sınırlı kalmayacağını, gelecekteki model ve yatırım kararlarını da etkileyeceğini ortaya koyuyor. Özellikle Wolfsburg gibi şirketin merkezinde yer alan bir fabrikada projelerin durdurulması, yönetim ile çalışanlar arasında devam eden görüşmelerin daha da zorlu geçebileceğine işaret ediyor.

news.title: Bir daha asla erişilemeyecek: Ukrayna İHA'larından Yandex kullanıcılarına darbe
news.summary: Yandex'in açıklamasına göre, insansız hava aracı saldırıları sonrasında bulut hizmeti müşterilerinin verilerinin yaklaşık yüzde 3'ü kalıcı olarak kayboldu.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Bir daha asla erişilemeyecek: Ukrayna İHA'larından Yandex kullanıcılarına darbe
news.summaryTr: Yandex'in açıklamasına göre, insansız hava aracı saldırıları sonrasında bulut hizmeti müşterilerinin verilerinin yaklaşık yüzde 3'ü kalıcı olarak kayboldu.
news.articleText: Bir daha asla erişilemeyecek: Ukrayna İHA'larından Yandex kullanıcılarına darbe - Yandex'in açıklamasına göre, insansız hava aracı saldırıları sonrasında bulut hizmeti müşterilerinin verilerinin yaklaşık yüzde 3'ü kalıcı olarak kayboldu. Yandex yaptığı açıklamada, geçen ay Ukrayna'nın veri merkezlerine düzenlediği insansız hava aracı saldırılarından etkilenen bulut müşteri verilerinin yaklaşık yüzde 97'sine erişimin yeniden sağlandığını, belirtti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Moscow Times'ta yer alan habere göre, şirket kalan yüzde 3'lük kısmın ise kalıcı olarak kaybolduğunu açıkladı. Teknoloji şirketi, yaptığı basın açıklamasında veri kaybını "ekipmanda meydana gelen kritik hasara" ve bazı bulut müşterilerinin platformda harici yedeklemeleri sürdürmemesine bağladı. Ukrayna insansız hava araçları, 8 Ekim ile 11 Ekim tarihleri arasında Yandex'in birçok veri merkezine saldırdı. Bu saldırılar, araç çağırma uygulamaları, araç paylaşım hizmetleri, yemek teslimatı ve çevrimiçi haritaların yanı sıra e-posta, bankacılık ve yayın platformlarında aksamalara yol açtı. Yandex altyapısını kullanan devlet kurumları ve özel şirketler de bu durumdan etkilendi. Yandex daha sonra kullanıcılar ve işletmeler için "temel özellikleri" geri yüklediğini, ancak mühendislerinin tüm hizmetlerini tekrar çevrimiçi hale getirmek için hala çalıştığını açıkladı. Şirket son basın açıklamasında, otomatik yedekleme özelliklerini etkinleştiren bulut müşterilerinin hiçbir veri kaybı yaşamadığını belirtti. Gelecekte yaşanabilecek aksaklıklara karşı önlem almak amacıyla Yandex, tüm yeni sanal bulut sunucuları için varsayılan olarak otomatik veri yedeklemeyi etkinleştiren bir platform güncellemesi yayınladı. Şirket ayrıca, mühendislerin tek bir lokasyona olan bağımlılığı azaltmak için Rusya genelindeki daha geniş ve daha merkezi olmayan bir veri tesisleri ağına bilgi işlem iş yüklerini yeniden dağıtmak için çalıştığını da ekledi. Yandex daha önce, hedef alınan tesislerden ikisinde bulunan özel süper bilgisayarlarının saldırılardan zarar görmeden kurtulduğunu ve o zamandan beri güvenli alternatif yerlere taşındığını doğrulamıştı.

news.summary: Mada Masr editor-in-chief Lina Attalah is being tried on the charge of "publishing false news" and potentially faces imprisonment.

news.titleTr: Egyptian journalist's retrial adjourned as UN warns of 'assaults on press freedom'
news.summaryTr: Mada Masr editor-in-chief Lina Attalah is being tried on the charge of "publishing false news" and potentially faces imprisonment.
news.articleText: Egyptian journalist's retrial adjourned as UN warns of 'assaults on press freedom' - Published A criminal court in Cairo has postponed the retrial of the prominent Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah, whose case has drawn international condemnation. Wednesday's opening hearing was adjourned until 18 November after defence lawyers representing the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr requested a new judge. The UN has warned of "widening assaults on press freedom by Egyptian authorities, including the targeting, persecution and harassment of independent journalists". Attalah told the BBC that a recent crackdown was meant to "send a chilling message" to "the very few newsrooms that are left". She warned: "Everybody should be careful, everybody should be scared, everybody should be wondering if they are next." Set up 13 years ago, Mada Masr became Egypt's leading independent news site with Attalah as its editor-in-chief and co-founder. Last month, another Cairo court convicted her of running a website without a licence - which she said she had tried in vain for years to obtain. She was issued a hefty fine of 3 million Egyptian pounds ($56,000; £42,000) and Mada Masr was ordered to shut down. After that trial, Attalah found that a court had previously given her a one-year prison sentence, without her knowledge, for "spreading false news" - a charge often used against journalists and dissidents - as well as operating a website without a licence. It was issued in absentia in 2024, even though she was in the country at the time. Attalah is now being retried in that case by the same judge. Egypt has largely stifled freedom of the press, ranking 169th out of 180 countries for press freedom, according to Reporters Without Borders' 2026 analysis. The group says that at least 26 journalists who were arrested in recent years remain in detention. While most newspapers and television stations now keep to government lines, Mada Masr remained a rare, independent and investigative news source in Egypt. However, since 2017 the site could only be viewed from outside the country. It had reported on alleged corruption and human rights abuses, and provided deep coverage of politics and economics, as well as regional upheaval and wars in Libya, Sudan and Gaza. In her BBC interview on Sunday, Attalah insisted that the factual reporting and professional standards of Mada Masr had an important role to play in Egyptian society, which could benefit the government. "It's much better if you have a little space left to have it open for professional media organisations who do rigorous reporting, because if we disappear, then you make the space for conspiracies and disinformation," she said. "People need to know, people need to consume information and you're shooting yourself in the foot if you're killing the newsrooms that do it properly." In September, six journalists with the independent fact-checking platform, Matsda2sh - constituting its entire newsroom - were arrested in home raids by the Egyptian authorities and held incommunicado for nearly a week. They have since been charged with joining the Muslim Brotherhood and financing terrorism, and their lawyers report that several were beaten and electrocuted in detention. They say that no evidence has been presented linking them to the Brotherhood. Egypt's former president Mohammed Morsi – who was backed by the Muslim Brotherhood – was removed from power by the military, led by Abdul Fattah al-Sisi, in July 2013 after widespread protests. Under Sisi, who became president the following year, the Islamist movement was classed as a terrorist organisation, leading to a widespread clampdown. On Tuesday, a spokesperson for the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Thameen Al-Kheetan, called for the Matsda2sh reporters to be released, with all charges dropped. He also said the case against Attalah "raises fresh concerns regarding due process and fair trial". "We call on Egypt to end all forms of harassment of journalists and media outlets, and to respect and fulfil the right to freedom of expression, including the right to information," Al-Kheetan said. "The steps taken to suppress the continued work of both Matsda2sh and Mada Masr must be overturned. The people of Egypt have a right to read and hear views expressed through these fora on issues of legitimate public concern." Attalah has suggested the authorities might again be trying to silence independent voices at a time of economic strain in Egypt and regional instability. It has been widely noted that recent legal action against journalists comes after the US State Department waived human rights conditions on $320m (£240m) in its foreign military funding for Egypt in September. This allowed the funds to be released as part of Washington's annual $1.3bn military aid package. The BBC asked US Secretary of State Marco Rubio whether he had raised the recent crackdown on independent journalism with Egypt's Foreign Minister, Badr Abdelatty, at their meeting about regional tensions in Paris on Monday. "We didn't discuss it today," Rubio said. "But… like anything else in foreign policy, there's always a balancing act to further the national interest of the United States. And in the end, Egypt has been a reliable and good defence partner of the United States." "That doesn't mean you agree with everything another government does," he went on, adding that he was not "opining about their journalists". news.titleTr: Zcash falls below $1,000 for first time since September
news.summaryTr: Zcash fell nearly 15% amid a broader sell-off in privacy coins, a day after Grayscale pledged $1 million to ecosystem initiatives.
news.articleText: Zcash falls below $1,000 for first time since September Zcash fell nearly 15% amid a broader sell-off in privacy coins, a day after Grayscale pledged $1 million to ecosystem initiatives. Zcash (ZEC) fell to a two-month low of $962.85 on Wednesday, a day after Grayscale pledged $1 million to nonprofits and projects supporting the Zcash network. As of 12:20 pm UTC Wednesday, Zcash’s 13.5% drop led 24-hour losses among the 100 largest cryptocurrencies by market capitalization and was down 24.5% over seven days. The decline was part of a broader crypto sell-off that left Bitcoin (BTC) down 5.8% and Ether (ETH) down 11.6% over the same period, according to CoinGecko. Crypto prices fell further Tuesday after US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October from the previous month, above economists’ 0.3% forecast. Zcash lets users send shielded payments that keep sender and recipient addresses and transaction amounts out of public view. Zcash helped drive this year’s rally in privacy coins, gaining 138% in the 30 days to Sept. 7. It remains the largest privacy coin by market value, accounting for about 60% of the $28 billion category tracked by CoinGecko. The category’s combined market value fell about 7% over 24 hours. ZEC traded above $1,370 as recently as Friday, when Zcash activated its NU7 upgrade. The upgrade cut the target time between blocks from 75 seconds to 25 to speed up transaction confirmations. It also made about 12,224 ZEC held in the network’s original privacy pool unspendable. Grayscale converted its Zcash Trust into a US spot exchange-traded fund (ETF) that began trading on NYSE Arca on Aug. 25. The fund recorded about $15 million in net outflows in November through Monday, following about $46 million in October, according to SoSoValue. Related: Zcash devs propose another block time cut days after NU7 upgrade

news.summary: Emails containing the false warnings were sent to schools in Rome, Naples, Vicenza, Florence, Pisa, Trieste and other Italian cities, officials say.

news.titleTr: Hundreds of Italian schools hit by threats in suspected bomb hoax
news.summaryTr: Emails containing the false warnings were sent to schools in Rome, Naples, Vicenza, Florence, Pisa, Trieste and other Italian cities, officials say.
news.articleText: Hundreds of Italian schools hit by threats in suspected bomb hoax - Published Some 300 schools across Italy have received bomb threats, according to Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara, who described the incidents as probably a "cyber-attack, not a genuine risk". Valditara told Italian TV that there was a clear strategy behind the rash of threats in Italy and elsewhere in Europe which had targeted flights, supermarkets and even hospitals. The emails were sent to schools in Rome, Naples, Vicenza, Florence, Pisa, Trieste and many other Italian cities, and a number of buildings were evacuated as a precaution. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has called a meeting of top ministers and intelligence chiefs. Meloni said the government was monitoring closely the "numerous reports of bomb threats at educational institutions" although checks so far had not indicated any evidence of "concrete danger". "These reports appear rather linked to a strategy intended to cause alarm and concern," she said on Facebook. Italian airports along with airlines elsewhere in Europe were hit by a series of bomb hoaxes last week that prompted a series of scares, evacuations and widespread disruption. Although a number of threats were claimed by an extremist misogynistic group, it later denied any link to the false warnings. Italian reports said 280 school head teachers had received threats in recent days. Although many schools were initially evacuated on Wednesday, the alarm was quickly lifted, according to reports from a number of regions, and pupils were allowed to return to class. In a statement, the head of the central Umbria region Stefania Proietti said "checks conducted so far in Umbrian schools have proved negative, and law enforcement is working rapidly and carefully to verify each report". In a separate incident, more than 300 schools in Northern Ireland were sent emails which police said they were treating as a hoax. Messages sent to number of schools in Scotland were also being treated by police as a hoax. It is unclear whether any of the incidents are connected. Related topics - Published5 days ago

news.titleTr: COP31'de duyuruldu: EBRD'den Türkiye'nin yenilenebilir enerji projelerine 6 milyar dolar yatırım
news.summaryTr: Antalya'da düzenlenen COP31 İklim Zirvesi'nde Türkiye'nin enerji dönüşümüne yönelik önemli bir yatırım planı gündeme geldi. Avrupa İmar ve Kalkınma Bankası'nın açıkladığı hedef, önümüzdeki beş yıllık dönemi kapsıyor.
news.articleText: COP31'de duyuruldu: EBRD'den Türkiye'nin yenilenebilir enerji projelerine 6 milyar dolar yatırım - EBRD, Türkiye'nin yenilenebilir enerji projelerine 5 yılda 6 milyar dolar yatırım yapmayı planlıyor. Avrupa İmar ve Kalkınma Bankası (EBRD), Türkiye'nin yenilenebilir enerji yatırımlarını hızlandırmak amacıyla oluşturduğu Yenilenebilir Enerjiyi Hızlandırma ve Temiz Dönüşüm Platformu'na (REACT) katıldığını ve gelecek 5 yılda platform kapsamındaki projelere 6 milyar dolar yatırım yapmayı planladığını duyurdu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle EBRD tarafından yapılan açıklamaya göre, REACT platformu Antalya'da düzenlenen COP31 İklim Zirvesi kapsamında gerçekleştirilen özel bir etkinlikle hayata geçirildi. Banka, platformun oluşturulması sürecinde Enerji ve Tabii Kaynaklar Bakanlığı ile yakın işbirliği içinde çalışarak aktif rol üstlendi. Platformun, 2040 yılına kadar yenilenebilir enerji değer zincirinde toplam 300 milyar dolarlık yatırımın harekete geçirilmesini sağlaması hedefleniyor. Söz konusu yatırımların yenilenebilir enerji üretimi, elektrik şebekesi altyapısı, enerji depolama, esneklik çözümleri, imalat ve elektrifikasyon alanlarını kapsaması öngörülüyor. Yatırım hedefleri, COP31 kapsamında belirlenen "35'e 35 Küresel Elektrifikasyon Taahhüdü" ile uyumlu şekilde oluşturuldu. REACT platformuna EBRD'nin yanı sıra Avrupa Birliği, Dünya Bankası, Uluslararası Finans Kurumu (IFC), Glasgow Net Sıfır Finans İttifakı (GFANZ), Uluslararası İmar ve Kalkınma Bankası (IBRD), İklim Yatırım Fonları (CIF), Alman Kalkınma Bankası (KfW), Kömürden Çıkış İttifakı (PPCA), Danimarka Kraliyet Büyükelçiliği ve Birleşmiş Milletler Sınai Kalkınma Teşkilatı (UNIDO) da destek veriyor.
